newsitem.title: USA: Richardson sees progress in U.N. payment talks.
newsitem.headline: Richardson sees progress in U.N. payment talks.

text.p: The Clinton administration was making progress in talks with Congress to free up funds to pay about $1 billion in United Nations back dues, U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Bill Richardson said on Saturday.
Appearing on CNN's "Evans and Novak" programme, Richardson said failure to pay that debt "would be a very, very catastrophic foreign policy blunder that will hurt America's interests."
"We're working very hard right now with Congress to find a package that pushes some serious reforms at the U.N., but at the same time, pays off our arrears," he said.

Richardson said there has been progress in the talks. He said the budget resolution worked out by Congress and the White House contained some money for paying the U.N. debts, although the amount of payment was being negotiated.
"...I think, in the end, the responsible Congress and an administration that wants to deal with this issue in a bipartisan basis -- I believe we will have a package," he said.

He said the White House agreed with Congress that the U.S. share of funding for the U.N. should be reduced to 20 percent from 25 percent, and that the U.N. needed reforms such as "less staff, less committees..."
